title: EoS marker handling + sampling-mode inheritance caused customer eval noise on Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Diego Morales
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported degraded eval parity and noisy outputs after the 2025-10 serving rollout. The regression appears across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments but manifests differently: Hosted customers see over-generation (models ignore explicit EoS markers embedded in prompt metadata), Dedicated deployments with fallbacks to compat models sometimes drop stop annotations during routing, and Private installs that use our config normalization step have prompts with end-of-sequence markers converted to neutral tokens. Root cause hypothesis: a config normalization change (internal flag eos_normalize=true) combined with a sampling-mode inheritance change in the runtime caused explicit EoS markers attached in request metadata to be deprioritized when merging per-request and per-model stop rules. In batched execution paths the token-emission precedence favored sampling policy directives over explicit stop markers when KV-cache/continuation logic merged multiple request contexts. Impact: customer evals that depend on deterministic termination or exact stop-token behavior show metric regressions (rouge/bleu drops, eval pass rate regressions up to 18% for several prompt sets). Immediate mitigation: rolled back eos_normalize across Hosted; applied routing patch to preserve stop metadata for Dedicated fallbacks; issued guidelines to Private customers for a temporary request header to enforce stop precedence. Next steps: implement deterministic stop-token precedence in runtime, add e2e regression tests that hit batching + fallback routings, and add monitoring alerting scoped to stop-token mismatch rates.
comments: 2025-10-28 - Diego Morales: SEV raised by two customers (enterprise/fin and ai-native search startup). Initial triage: reproduce with canonical prompts; observed model continues past explicit EOS markers when request includes per-request stop list in metadata object instead of in top-level request body.

2025-10-29 - Priya Nair: Reproduced in staging with deduped prompt set. Root-cause candidate: config normalizer commit 7a1b2c3 (eos_normalize=true) merged in runtime config service; sampling inheritance change (ENG-33450) altered merge order of per-request and model defaults.

2025-10-30 - Aisha Kumar (SRE): Rolled back eos_normalize flag in hosted control plane at 2025-10-30T03:12Z. Early telemetry shows hosted over-generation decreased by ~10% for affected customers. Dedicated patch queued.

2025-11-01 - Priya Nair: Hotfix PR submitted: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892 - "ensure-stop-precedence-in-emission-path". The fix enforces: explicit per-request stop tokens > model config stop tokens > sampling termination heuristics. Added unit tests for emission precedence; still lacking e2e tests for batching interactions.

2025-11-03 - QA (Liam O'Connor): Verified hotfix locally against batching harness with 32 concurrent contexts; still observed a rare race where fallback routing path copied stop metadata into fallback context after sampling policy applied. Created a small repro harness and opened follow-up bug ENG-33705.

2025-11-05 - Customer liaison (Sofia Park): Sent interim communication to affected customers summarizing rollback and mitigation steps; provided temporary header X-RWD-STOP-PRECEDENCE=true for Private customers to opt in. Collected three customer prompt samples for regression suite inclusion.

2025-11-07 - Priya Nair: Deployed hotfix to Hosted (canary 5% then 50%) with new metric stop_token_mismatch_rate. Observed reduction to baseline for canary traffic. Preparing Dedicated and Private rollout plan with kube-operator migration notes.

2025-11-10 - Diego Morales: Post-deploy check: hosted customers who reported the issue have pass rates restored to within 2% of baseline. Dedicated customer awaiting scheduled maintenance window for full rollout. Private installs have guidance and temp header; working with onsite engineer to schedule upgrade. Marking ticket to keep open until Dedicated/Private complete and regression suite added.

Instructions for on-call: If new customer reports similar symptoms, collect the raw request payload, the effective merged stop list from the routing trace, and the model variant used. Attach routing trace ID and time window.
qa_plan: Add targeted e2e tests that run batching harness with mixed per-request stop lists and fallback routing; create nightly job that replays customer prompt samples against current runtime to detect deviations; add unit tests for precedence merge logic; run dedicated cluster upgrade in canary before tenant-wide rollout.
acceptance_criteria: 1) stop_token_mismatch_rate back to baseline for canary and then global traffic; 2) Dedicated rolling upgrade completes without routing-induced metadata loss; 3) Regression suite covers at least 10 customer prompt sets and fails if outputs deviate by >3% on eval pass rate; 4) Documentation and developer notes published in runtime README.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-33900 - update private upgrade playbook and add header gating
communication_notes: Interim customer message templates in Confluence. Postmortem scheduled 2025-11-18. Legal/CS teams looped for top-tier customers. Billing not impacted; offered engineering credits to two affected customers pending final RCA.
notes_for_release: Include a runtime changelog entry emphasizing stop-token precedence fix and the temporary header option for private deployments. Coordinate release notes with Console and Dedicated upgrade schedule.
resolution_summary: Hotfix PR merged and deployed to Hosted canary on 2025-11-07; rollback of eos_normalize prevented further regressions in Hosted. Ongoing work to fix fallback race and complete Dedicated/Private rollouts. Evaluation metrics recovering for reported customers.
